_meta: Per-topic index of the R30-R34 notes. 'cite' = PDF pages; 'terms' = terms that must appear on those pages (checked by tests/verify_citations.py). All items are [from source].

features.name: Ractor (Ruby 3.0, experimental)
features.summary: Actor-style concurrency abstraction; ractors do not share normal objects and exchange messages; experimental, with a warning on the first Ractor.new; the example measures 3.87x with 4 ractors.

features.name: Ractor in Ruby 3.4
features.summary: require allowed inside a Ractor (runs in the main one), Ractor._require, Ractor.main?, Ractor.[] and []=, Ractor.store_if_absent; YJIT supports shareable constants in multi-ractor mode.

features.name: Fiber Scheduler
features.summary: Fiber#scheduler intercepts blocking operations (Mutex, Queue, Thread#join, sleep, Process.wait, IO#read/write/wait...); IO#select is not supported; example with the async gem.

features.name: M:N thread scheduler
features.summary: M Ruby threads on top of N native threads; disabled in the main Ractor by default (RUBY_MN_THREADS=1 enables it); RUBY_MAX_CPU defaults to 8.

features.name: Ruby 3x3 goal
features.summary: Ruby 3 three times faster than Ruby 2 on some benchmarks (Optcarrot); 3.1 says the JIT did not benefit real business applications.

features.name: MJIT
features.summary: Method-based JIT with an external C compiler; limited to certain workloads in 3.0, not ready for Rails; reimplemented in Ruby in 3.2; replaced by RJIT in 3.3. [DATED]

features.name: YJIT (3.1, experimental)
features.summary: Shopify's in-process JIT; LBBV; up to 22% on railsbench and 39% on liquid-render; experimental, disabled by default, --yjit, Unix-like x86-64 only.

features.name: YJIT production-ready (3.2)
features.summary: No longer experimental; x86-64 and arm64 on Linux/macOS/BSD/Unix; building requires Rust 1.58+; 41% faster on yjit-bench; about 1/3 of the memory overhead; Code GC; defaults 64 MiB and threshold 30.

features.name: YJIT in 3.3
features.summary: More than 3x the interpreter on Optcarrot; threshold goes from 30 to 120 with more than 40,000 ISEQs; Code GC off by default; RubyVM::YJIT.enable at runtime.

features.name: YJIT in 3.4
features.summary: --yjit-mem-size (unified limit, 128 MiB), --yjit-log and RubyVM::YJIT.log, compressed context, Array#each/select/map in Ruby, inlining of trivial methods.

features.name: RJIT
features.summary: Pure-Ruby JIT that replaced MJIT; Unix x86-64 only; no C compiler at runtime; experimental; keep using YJIT in production.

features.name: GC improvements (3.3)
features.summary: Young objects are not promoted immediately; new limit (default 0.01); write barriers and VWA in more classes; weak references; RUBY_GC_HEAP_INIT_SLOTS deprecated.

features.name: Modular GC (3.4)
features.summary: Alternative GCs loaded through RUBY_GC_LIBRARY; default GC split out; experimental MMTk library (Rust); GC.config.

features.name: RBS
features.summary: Language for describing types: classes, modules, unions, overloading, generics, interfaces; rbs gem; 3.1: bounded generics, generic aliases, rbs collection.

features.name: TypeProf
features.summary: Generates a prototype of RBS signatures from unannotated code (typeprof test.rb); experimental in 3.0; TypeProf for IDE (VS Code) in 3.1.

features.name: Pattern matching in 3.0
features.summary: => as rightward assignment; in returns a boolean; find pattern (experimental); case/in is no longer experimental.

features.name: Pattern matching in 3.1/3.2
features.summary: Pin ^ accepts an expression; optional parentheses in one-line form; one-line is no longer experimental (3.1); find pattern is no longer experimental (3.2).

features.name: Endless method
features.summary: def square(x) = x * x.

features.name: Argument forwarding `...`
features.summary: In 3.0, ... starts accepting leading arguments (def method_missing(meth, ...)).

features.name: Keyword argument separation
features.summary: Keywords are separated from positional arguments; in principle, code that warned in 2.7 does not work.

features.name: Value omission in Hash/keywords
features.summary: {x:, y:} is equivalent to {x: x, y: y}; foo(x:, y:) is equivalent to foo(x: x, y: y).

features.name: Anonymous * and ** arguments (3.2)
features.summary: Anonymous * and ** can be forwarded; a proc with one positional argument and keywords no longer autosplats.

features.name: ruby2_keywords mandatory (3.2)
features.summary: Methods that delegate keywords through *args must be marked with ruby2_keywords, without exception.

features.name: Data
features.summary: Simple immutable value class, similar to Struct, with a leaner and stricter API; with; no setters.

features.name: Struct with keywords (3.2)
features.summary: Struct.new accepts keyword initialization without keyword_init: true.

features.name: Built-in Set (3.2)
features.summary: Set available without require; autoloaded through the Set constant or Enumerable#to_set.

features.name: Parameter `it`
features.summary: 3.3: it without arguments in a block with no parameters is deprecated; 3.4: it references the block parameter, like _1.

features.name: Warning when mutating a string literal (3.4)
features.summary: In files without a frozen_string_literal comment, mutating a literal emits a deprecation warning (-W:deprecated); --disable-frozen-string-literal turns it off.

features.name: Prism
features.summary: 3.3: default gem, error-tolerant recursive-descent parser; 3.4: default parser (--parser=parse.y for the old one).

features.name: Lrama
features.summary: LALR parser generator that replaced Bison (Feature #19637).

features.name: debug gem
features.summary: Rewritten debugger: remote, VS Code and Chrome, multi-process/thread, colored REPL, record & replay; replaces lib/debug.rb.

features.name: error_highlight
features.summary: Fine-grained location in the backtrace; in 3.1 only NameError; enabled by default; in 3.2 it points at the argument in TypeError and ArgumentError.

features.name: SyntaxSuggest
features.summary: Integrates syntax_suggest (formerly dead_end) to find a missing or extra end.

features.name: WebAssembly/WASI
features.summary: Initial port to WebAssembly/WASI; passes the basic and bootstrap suites without the Thread API; Asyncify for Fiber, exceptions and GC; VFS to bundle into .wasm.

features.name: ReDoS: memoization algorithm
features.summary: Regexp matching with memoization: example goes from 10 s to 0.003 s; ~90% in linear time; memory up to ~10x the input.

features.name: Regexp.timeout
features.summary: Fallback for regexes with back-references, look-around or huge repetitions; Regexp.timeout = 1.0 (global) raises Regexp::TimeoutError; timeout: in Regexp.new per regex; Float::INFINITY turns the limit off.

features.name: Regexp.new with 2 arguments (3.3)
features.summary: Regexp.new accepts at most 2 arguments (deprecated in 3.2).

features.name: $SAFE removed (3.0)
features.summary: $SAFE removed; now an ordinary global variable.

features.name: Backtrace order (3.0)
features.summary: The 2.5 inversion was reverted: error and line first, callers afterwards (as in 2.4).

features.name: Removals in 3.2
features.summary: Removed Fixnum, Bignum, Random::DEFAULT, Struct::Group/Passwd, Dir.exists?, File.exists?, Kernel#=~, taint/trust and related methods.

features.name: Error format and Hash#inspect (3.4)
features.summary: Single quotes instead of backtick, class name before the method; Hash#inspect with {user: 1} and {"user" => 1}.

features.name: Happy Eyeballs v2 (3.4)
features.summary: TCPSocket.new and Socket.tcp resolve IPv6/IPv4 in parallel and try connections staggered every 250 ms; enabled by default.

features.name: Psych 4.0 (3.1)
features.summary: Psych.load uses safe_load by default; Psych 3.3.2 helps with migration.

features.name: Default gems that become bundled
features.summary: 3.1: net-ftp/imap/pop/smtp, matrix, prime, debug; 3.3: require warnings for abbrev, base64, bigdecimal, csv, drb and others; 3.4: mutex_m, getoptlong, base64, bigdecimal, observer, abbrev, csv, drb...

features.name: Libraries dropped in 3.0
features.summary: sdbm, webrick, net-telnet and xmlrpc stop being bundled gems or part of the stdlib; install the gem.

features.name: IRB
features.summary: Pasting code 53x faster and measure (3.0); autocomplete (3.1); debug and Pry-like commands (3.2); irb:rdbg and pager (3.3).

features.name: AbstractSyntaxTree: error_tolerant and keep_tokens
features.summary: RubyVM::AbstractSyntaxTree.parse accepts error_tolerant and keep_tokens.

features.name: PubGrub in Bundler 2.4
features.summary: Bundler 2.4 uses PubGrub; RubyGems keeps Molinillo in 3.2.

features.name: Timeout.timeout rejects negative values (3.4)
features.summary: Negative values are now rejected.

features.name: Faster JSON.parse (3.4)
features.summary: JSON.parse about 1.5x faster than json-2.7.x.

features.name: Refinement#refined_class
features.summary: Added in 3.2 and removed in 3.4.

features.name: URI with RFC 3986 (3.4)
features.summary: The default URI parser moves from RFC 2396 to RFC 3986.

features.name: Net::HTTP constants removed (3.4)
features.summary: Constants deprecated since 2012 were removed.

features.name: ext/readline retired (3.3)
features.summary: Use reline; ext/readline via the readline-ext gem.

features.name: libyaml and libffi no longer bundled (3.2)
features.summary: psych and fiddle no longer ship the libyaml and libffi code.

features.name: 3.4 warnings in verbose and performance mode
features.summary: A block passed to a method that does not use it warns with -w; redefining String.freeze or Integer#+ warns with -W:performance.

features.name: Memory view, Hash#except and others (3.0)
features.summary: Memory view (experimental C API); native Hash#except.

not_covered.note: GVL/GIL do not appear in the five notes; 'without the GVL' is [extrapolation]. What the note says: parallel execution without thread-safety concerns (R30 p.2).
Rules for shareable objects and Ractor ownership transfer are not in the notes; they only point to doc/ractor.md (R30 p.3).
The notes talk about Fiber#scheduler (R30 p.3), not Fiber.set_scheduler.
The RUBY_YJIT_ENABLE variable and application servers do not appear in the notes; use --yjit (R31 p.2) or RubyVM::YJIT.enable (R33 p.3).
They do not appear in the five notes (byebug only appears as pry-byebug in R33 p.6, when describing irb:rdbg).
FrozenError does not appear in the notes; 3.4 only emits a deprecation warning when a literal is mutated (R34 p.5).
The notes cover 3.0 to 3.4. The captures only show 4.0.x in Recent News (R30 p.10; R34 p.12). [DATED]
Only passing mentions of Rails (R31 p.1, p.8; R33 p.3, p.7); Rails itself is not covered.
